## Why This Is Asked
This question tests choosing an architecture that stays Open-Closed, supports runtime extension of handlers, and keeps the ingestion core simple and testable.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy/Polymorphism
- Open-Closed Principle
- Registry-based dispatch

## Code Example
```javascript
interface FormatHandler { parse(input) }
class JsonHandler implements FormatHandler { parse(input) { /* parse JSON */ } }
class Ingestor { constructor(registry) { this.registry = registry } ingest(format, data) { return this.registry[format].parse(data) } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle unknown formats at runtime?
- How would you test individual handlers and end-to-end ingestion?

## Why This Is Asked
Introduce a new angle: runtime-extensible evaluation logic for feature flags to reflect real-world needs in large orgs.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for evaluators
- Registry for dynamic extension
- Composite rule composition (anyOf/allOf)
- EvalContext design and caching for performance

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Evaluator { evaluate(ctx: EvalContext): boolean }
type EvalContext = { user: any; time: Date; attrs: any }
class EvaluatorRegistry {
  register(name: string, factory: (cfg: any)=>Evaluator): void
  resolve(name: string, cfg: any): Evaluator
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to model evaluation order and short-circuit semantics?
- How to handle cross-feature conflicts and auditing of evaluator registrations?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to extend behavior without touching core dispatch logic; demonstrates the Command pattern with a runtime registry.

## Key Concepts
- Command pattern
- Registry-based extensibility
- Safe, non-invasive extension

## Code Example
```javascript
interface Command { execute(args: string[]): void; }
class Registry { private map = new Map<string, Command>(); register(name: string, c: Command) { this.map.set(name, c); } get(name: string): Command | undefined { return this.map.get(name); } }
class Router { constructor(private registry: Registry) {} route(argv: string[]) { const cmd = argv[0]; const command = this.registry.get(cmd); if (command) command.execute(argv.slice(1)); else throw new Error('Unknown command'); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle asynchronous commands? 
- How would you ensure thread-safety in a multi-process CLI?

## Why This Is Asked
Beginner-friendly exploration of extensibility and non-blocking I/O: add new sinks without changing core, and isolate failures per sink.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy/Plug-in pattern for runtime extension
- Registry mapping names to Sink implementations
- Non-blocking writes via per-sink queuing and worker pool
- Fault isolation and graceful degradation

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Sink { write(msg: string): Promise<void> }
class Registry { addSink(name: string, s: Sink): void; getSinks(): Sink[] }
class Logger { constructor(private reg: Registry) ; log(msg: string): void { for (const s of reg.getSinks()) s.write(msg); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test sink isolation and backpressure?
- How would you implement graceful shutdown for all sinks?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design extensible, runtime-extendable components with minimal coupling using Strategy + Registry patterns.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy: encapsulate evaluation logic per flag
- Registry/Plugin: dynamic, runtime-extensible factories
- Dependency Injection: decouples engine from evaluators
- Thread-safety and versioning considerations for runtime extensions

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Context { tenantId: string; userId: string; region?: string; [key: string]: any }
interface Evaluator { evaluate(ctx: Context): boolean }
interface EvaluatorFactory { create(): Evaluator }
class Registry { private map = new Map<string, EvaluatorFactory>(); register(n: string, f: EvaluatorFactory) { this.map.set(n, f) } getFactory(n: string): EvaluatorFactory | undefined { return this.map.get(n) } }
class FlagEngine { constructor(private registry: Registry) {} isEnabled(flag: string, ctx: Context): boolean { const f = this.registry.getFactory(flag); if (!f) throw new Error(`Unknown flag: ${flag}`); return f.create().evaluate(ctx); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle hot-reload of strategies without restarting the service?
- How would you version/evolve evaluator interfaces while keeping backward compatibility?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Demonstrates open-closed extensibility by adding formats without changing the converter.

## Key Concepts

- Strategy pattern
- Registry / Plugin pattern
- Open/Closed Principle

## Code Example

```javascript
interface Format {
  parse(str) 
  serialize(data)
}
class JsonFormat implements Format { /* ... */ }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle format versioning?
- How to ensure thread-safe registry access in concurrent runs?
